status: Reviewed R1-R5 against current limits, allocation/owner boundaries, representative API contracts and installed host consumers. The absorbed HTTP/host handoff acceptance is revalidated.

inspected: Input bytes and expanded XML reader characters are independently bounded; element count, depth and attributes are checked through ordinary, retained and inert-subtree traversal.
Output rounding/fitting retains dimension, pixel and contiguous-RGBA limits before allocation. Embedded images and filter source/halo frames enforce their own surface bounds.
Path command limits are cumulative across supported path elements and checked before expansion; generated geometry has bounded builders.
Encoded-size checks include fixed PNG/chunk overhead and bounded IDAT slices for owned, caller-memory and stream sinks.
These are structural/storage bounds. No synthetic parse/raster/encoder work allowance replaces cooperative cancellation.
R1.checks: Direct dimension/raster/PNG/decoder boundaries, cumulative parser limits and representative destination contracts; pixels have separate native owners.

inspected: The host root is borrowed. Empty scopes introduce no independent cap; reservation and growth refusal preserve existing charges.
Array/list/dictionary growth and exact-array transfer reserve replacement capacity while old storage remains charged. Charges transfer with retained owners and release once.
PNG scanline/chunk/compressed/output storage has distinct peak and retained owners; caller-owned program/destination bytes remain borrowed.
Accounting is an estimate of dominant storage. Small metadata/runtime overhead and the documented approximate allowance are not a per-workload heap guarantee.
R2.checks: Zero/negative/disposed admission, failed growth, shared roots, parser capacity, scene transfer, rendering denial, encoding growth and immediate reuse.

inspected: Tokens flow through discovery, program acquisition, parsing, raster work, PNG scanlines/CRC/copies and awaited destination writes.
Operation cleanup encloses real async completion. Cancellation does not refund a still-running borrowed byte read or destination write.
Encoder failure aborts further compression output and releases scratch. Borrowed streams/clients/root budgets are not disposed; output transactions belong to the host.
Failure/refusal/cancellation unwind partial scene/font/execution owners; later independent operations can reuse allowance.
R3.checks: Held byte reads, async backpressure/write failure, partial row/scan cancellation, acquisition cancellation, denied storage and retry after cleanup.

inspected: Snapshot programs are borrowed immutable byte regions; callers serialize disposal with readers. Disposal invalidates retained prepared faces and drops metadata/requests.
Prepared conversion admission uses one atomic state transition. Its synchronous and asynchronous paths release retained scene/snapshot storage after the sole attempt completes.
Owned PNG results use a sibling scope beneath the borrowed host owner, outlive operation/document cleanup and release bytes/charge on result disposal.
Caller serialization and parent lifetime remain explicit contracts; the library does not infer reader completion from disposal alone.
R4.checks: Shared snapshots, governed bare-memory rejection without consuming the document, retained result competition, independent sibling lifetime and overlapping async output.

inspected: Governed bare-memory output rejects; owned/memory/stream destinations keep appropriate result versus scratch owners.
Prepared HTTP documents discover requirements once before catalog work. Font-free requests stay independent of cold, stalled or failed initialization.
Shared catalog/program loads retain resolver-owned deadlines and verified bytes. Waiter cancellation ends that wait without canceling another borrower.

The host supplies the root, client, transport policy and budgets sharing one allowance. Operation/result scopes use the supplied document owner; cache uses the resolver owner. Root ancestry is a host contract, not an identity heuristic.
Finite transient transport retry is distinct from later-call recovery. Size/integrity/deterministic failures and admission refusal do not retry.
Idle-capacity maintenance may trim unborrowed programs; refusal does not trigger eviction, waiting, alternate fonts or another storage path. Active borrowers keep cache charges through shutdown.
R5.checks: HTTP coalescing/selective acquisition, complete deadline/body handling, rooted paths, structured failures, borrowed client, zero-idle lifetime, shutdown, one preparation and installed public-package flows.
